page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Running head at the top centre. Page number at the top right. A marginal note at the right, beside the German fish names in the second paragraph. A catchword "CAP." alone at the lower right.

main_text.p: differre autem albos ab atris: viridium vero carnem macriorem, aridiorem, tenuiorisq; succi esse, & pinguitudinis expertes. Diocles saxatiles gobios mollioris esse carnis dixit, quod tamen Galenus mullorum respectu vult esse verum, ait enim, gobionum caro saxatilium carne durior est, & mollior, quam mullorum.

Pisces candidi, Leucisci, Alburni, ger-man. dicuntur Weißfische / Gleißling/àAlburn*. squamarum splendore, Zwibelfischlein/ quod nimirum cum cœpis coquantur, Roß-äuglein/ ab oculis rubicundis, & à vilitate Schneiderfischlein/ item Breitling à corporis latitudine. Meminit horum Aufonius, cum inquit,

Porro carnes eorum molles sunt & pituitosæ. Certum est aquis exemtos diutiusq; seruatos cito corrumpi, vitus[?] enim quoddam redolent, id quod odore facile cognoscitur ventre refecto interaneisque exemtis. Ex jure autem piperato non inutiliter edun-tur.
Adhuc de alimentis quæ veniunt ab a-nimalibus sanguineis simplicis vitæ, sequuntur amphibia, quæ ancipitis sunt naturæ, vt ranæ, lutra, fiber.

page.notes: The long s is printed as s throughout. Fraktur words are set in black letter inside the roman text and are marked with bl. The word "vitus" in "vitus enim" is doubtful; it is probably "virus", but the print reads as "vitus". The marginal note "Alburn*." is at the right beside "Gleißling". The page has stains and show-through from the other side, which are not transcribed.
